title: Oklahoma National Guard's civil support team practices rope rescues
description: Oklahoma National Guard members of the 63rd Civil Support Team, conduct ropes rescue technician training held Jan. 8, 2019 at the High Plains Technology Center in Woodward, Oklahoma. The training is part of an annual refresher and re-certification for unit members who continually train on aspects that directly affect their mission of being the Oklahoma National Guard’s team of first responders. The event included the basics of rope rescue from knot tying, to the more advanced portion of rappelling down and up a steep, simulated cliff.

transcript.text: - [Narrator] Soldiers and airmen from the Oklahoma
National Guard's 63rd Civil Support Team conducted
rope rescue training in Woodward, Oklahoma,
Tuesday, January 8th.
- Our main mission today is just to learn how to be able
to lower somebody down using ropes from a high point,
and also to be able to raise them back up.
- [Narrator] The week-long training is part of an annual
refresher, and recertification for the service members,
who continual train on all tasks needed
to complete their mission as first responders.
The training included the basics of rope rescue
from knot tying to the more advanced portion
of repelling down and up a steep, simulated cliff.
- Most of what we do will be in a emergency setting,
and so if for some reason during our normal mission
that we need to rescue one of our own people,
we have the abilities to rescue them.
Another time that we'd be able to use the ropes
to rescue training, would be to augment a search
and rescue team like Task Force 1
throughout the Oklahoma region as well.
- [Narrator] The 63rd CST's mission includes supporting
civil authorities during incidents with the ability
to identify chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear,
and explosive agents, or substances.
Assessing current and projected consequences, advising
on response measures, and assisting with appropriate
requests for additional state support.
Reporting from Woodward, Oklahoma,
I'm Army sergeant Michael Adams.
